Wraparound
Wraparound Care at St George’s Infant School
Our wraparound care is proudly delivered by All Kids Active, providing a safe, happy and energising place for your child before and after the school day. Booking is quick and easy - simply create an iPal account at this link or email our friendly team at info@allkidsactive.co.uk if you’d like any help or further information. You can also visit our website here which has more information on us as a company and FAQ’s.
We accept children in years Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
Breakfast Club – A Bright Start to Their Day
Breakfast Club runs from 7:30am until the start of school, giving children a calm but fun start to the morning. We offer both a 7:30am and 8am drop off at differing price points. We serve a healthy, nutritious breakfast to set them up for the day, and children can choose from a range of morning activities - quiet crafts, gentle games, building challenges and more. It’s the perfect mix of relaxing and engaging, helping them ease into the school day with a smile.
After-School Club – Fun, Friends and Fresh Experiences
Our after-school sessions run from the end of the school day until 6pm, and you can choose flexible pick-up times at 4:15pm, 5pm or 6pm. All sessions are available for regular or ad-hoc bookings, making it easy to fit childcare around your family’s schedule.
We offer a huge variety of activities every afternoon so there’s always something to look forward to.
Sports and active games led by our trained coaches
Creative crafts and hands-on projects
Team games, imaginative play and themed activities
Quiet spaces for reading, colouring or relaxing
Outdoor play, weather permitting
Children receive a fruit snack on arrival to refuel after their school day, and for added convenience, parents can purchase a light tea option if you would like your child to have something more substantial before heading home.
A Safe, Caring and Fun Environment
Our staff are warm, experienced and enthusiastic about giving children a brilliant experience every day. We focus on creating a supportive environment where children feel safe, confident and excited to try new things, all while spending time with friends.
Whether you need care every day or just once in a while, we’re here to help. We look forward to welcoming your child to All Kids Active at St George’s!
Our after-school Wraparound care is provided by All Kids Active. To book you will first need to create an account and register at this link All Kids Active iPAL Bookings or you can email us at info@allkidsactive.co.uk for further information.
There will be a range of sports, activities, games, crafts and experiences for them to join in with throughout the provision. Children will be provided with a fruit snack on arrival at the club and there is the option for parents to purchase a light tea option for an additional charge.

Safeguarding
At St George's Infant and Preschool, we take the safety and welfare of our pupils very seriously. Safeguarding is paramount and we maintain a safeguarding culture. Staff are expected to be 'professionally curious' in order to protect children.
Report a Concern About a Child
If you have a serious concern about a child, call Bucks First Response - 01296 383962
You can also contact one of the Designated Safeguarding Leads listed below.

Safeguarding Statement
Safeguarding is everybody's responsibility. Children have a right to be cared for and protected, this is everyone's responsibility. At St George's CE Infant and Preschool we recognise we have a duty of care to ensure our whole school community are kept safe from harm. We are committed to providing a safe and nurturing environment in which children can develop and grow to reach their full potential and flourish. Safeguarding children is an essential part of our holistic approach to ensure that children are protected to enable them to have the best outcomes.
At St George’s Church of England Infant and Preschool, we listen carefully to our pupils and take what they tell us, seriously. Our aim is for children to enjoy their time as pupils at this school. We want to work in partnership with you to help your child achieve their full potential and flourish.
To promote a safe environment for pupils, our selection and recruitment policy includes all checks on staff and regular volunteers’ suitability, including Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, as recommended by Buckinghamshire Council, in accordance with current legislation.
In accordance with our responsibilities under section 175/157 of the Education Act 2002 and “Keeping Children Safe in Education” Sept 2024, we have a Designated Safeguarding Lead for Child Protection (Victoria Harjette) who is the Head Teacher. All St George's staff, irrespective of whether their role is in direct contact with children or not, receive child protection awareness training on a regular basis.
Occasions do arise when our concern about a child might mean we have to consult other agencies. Whilst we would always aim to work in partnership with parents, there may be exceptions to this when concerns are raised for the protection of a child.
On very rare occasions, Social Care, whilst undertaking an investigation under S47 of the Children Act 1989, may want to speak to a child without a parents’ knowledge. This would be a decision made in collaboration with partner agencies and would only be done in situations where a child might be at immediate risk. To gain consent at this point may increase the level of risk to the child or cause evidence of a crime to be lost.
We cannot safeguard children alone. All children's services agencies work in partnership with each other. Parents and Carers can support this process too because everybody has a responsibility to safeguard children within their community and report concerns. If you have concerns about the safety of a child, please contact First Response (01296 383962) or speak to one of the designated safeguarding team at school. If a child is in immediate danger please phone 999.
The procedures we follow, are in accordance with the Local Safeguarding Children’s Board and Buckinghamshire Council. The school has adopted a Child Protection Policy in line with this for the safety of all. If you want to know more about our procedures, please speak to the Head Teacher (Victoria Harjette) or your child’s class teacher. This policy can be found here alongside our other safeguarding policies:
Educate Against Hate Website
The ‘Educate Against Hate’ website offers parents, teachers and school leaders practical advice to protect children from the dangers of extremism, drawing on resources and guidance designed by the government and charities such as the NSPCC and Childnet.
The Educate Against Hate website is here: Educate Against Hate
E-Safety
Internet Safety is really important to us at St George's. The Internet is a fantastic resource for discovering, communicating and creating.
We want to ensure that we teach a balanced view of these amazing new technologies - recognising the wonderful opportunities that they represent and teaching the children to use them well, whilst understanding the dangers and how to stay safe.
CPOMS
To help staff record and analyse behaviour we use an online recording system. This is called CPOMS and allows staff to spot behaviour trends, develop appropriate strategies and manage behaviour more effectively. This system allows staff to discuss with students and their carers their progress as well as monitor the effectiveness of interventions.

Pupil Voice and Responsibilities
At St George’s, we believe every child has a voice and a valuable contribution to make to our school community. Through a range of pupil leadership roles and responsibilities, children have opportunities to share their ideas, make a difference and develop confidence, responsibility and a sense of belonging. From helping to shape school life to representing their house, leading worship and championing sustainability, our pupils are encouraged to let their light shine.

PTA
Welcome to the Parent Teacher Association (PTA)
Registered charity: 298920
The Parent Teacher Association (PTA) is led by parents, supported by teachers and exists to raise money for the school. In order to achieve this, we hold a number of events throughout the year such as Summer fayres, Tea with Santa, Elfridges, school discos, Mother's Day & Father's day events, Cake sales, Break the rules day, and many more. We also raise money using the Voucher Scheme (see below for further details), School Lottery, Fund Matching Scheme, Asda cashpot for schools and Easyfundraising.
St George’s PTA Team:
Co-Secretaries: Sam Sanders & Aaron Williamson
Treasurer: Sarika Kinash
Our goal is to ensure that all children at St George's are given equal opportunities and have the best start to school life that they can. The funds we raise help to buy equipment for use in the classrooms, improve the teaching facilities and the school buildings, and give the children little treats along the way.
Please sign up to Classlist (www.classlist.com) for regular updates, events sign up, and online payments. Also, look out for Knights News in your email inbox!
This could not happen without the invaluable support from all of our parents and we are really keen to encourage everyone to help in whatever way they can. If you have a skill or hobby that could benefit the team such as cake making, artistic flair, DIY, photography, disco DJ, marketing, accounting or anything else, then please let us know. Or perhaps you have a local contact who could potentially support, assist, donate or sponsor events, or have a matched giving scheme within your company – again, we would love to hear from you. We are very grateful and fortunate to have such a diverse community at St. George's and welcome fresh perspectives, ideas, and contributions from everyone, no matter how small. Every little counts! In addition to raising funds, the PTA also aims to bring the community of St George’s together, with the hope of making it a really fun place to be, so come along and make new friends as you help raise money for the school. Email us at stgeorgesptateam@gmail.com if you'd like to get involved.

School Day
Main School (Reception and Key Stage 1)
School starts at 8.30 a.m. School finishes at 3.00 p.m.
Our School Day runs from 8.30am until 3.00pm each school day. We offer a Sensory Circuit Morning Club which runs from 8.35am until 8.45am. The school runs staff led clubs from Tuesday to Friday, 3.00pm until 3.30pm. This amounts to a total of 32.5 hours a week.
The whistle is blown at 8.30am the children can then go into class. Parents are responsible for their children until this whistle is blown. Children arriving after 8.35am are late and parents/carers will need to report to the office.
Our routines
An example day in Key Stage 1
8.30am – 8.50am – Registration and early morning work
8.55am – 9.15am – Collective worship
9.15am – 9.50am – Phonics
9.50am - 10.50am - Lesson 1
10.50am – 11.15am – Playtime and Daily Mile
11.15am - 12.15pm - Lesson 2
12.15pm – 1.15pm – Lunch (see School Meals)
1.15pm - 3.00pm - Afternoon Lessons
Preschool
Preschool hours differ depending on the sessions your child is booked onto. Please see the Preschool page for more information.
Attendance
Parents are encouraged not to take children on holiday during term time. We suggest you read the letter regarding absence and attendance when considering this. Requests for leave for holidays should be made in writing to Miss Victoria Harjette Head Teacher, to the school office or via email to office@st-georges.bucks.sch.uk for more information about term time absence please see our Attendance page and the Attendance Policy on the Policies Page (please see the links below).

Lunchtime
The Government Grant enabling all infant aged children access to a school meal has hugely benefited the children at St George's.
Please remember there is no charge for school aged children lunches and we require all children to have a Kids Lunch Company provided meal or packed lunch from home.
If your child will bring a home packed lunch, this must be a NUT FREE lunch.
Preschool children are welcome to order from the Kids Lunch Company but they will have to pay the daily charge per meal.
Please see the link below to order your child's lunches.
Please note the cut off for weekly orders is every Friday at midday.
